currentCoordinate.coordNote: Kameraposisjonen -28.679172, -49.376008 dokumenterer en synlig strekning ved Rua Henrique Lage. Hele stedet er lineært og trenger kilde-, segment- og sammenløpsgeometri før koordinatstatus kan verifiseres.

identity.resolvedIdentity: The named urban river from the Cruzeiro do Sul–Mina Brasil source area to its confluence with Rio Sangão
identity.splitReason: Open channels, closed conduits, culverts and natural reaches are parts of one named main river.

requiredEvidence: inspectable river centreline or route segments
at least one safe public observation point

evidence.finding: Municipal law 7.604/2019 approved a dedicated socioenvironmental diagnosis for the Rio Criciúma main channel.
evidence.reason: The law resolves the regulated river identity but does not provide the complete line geometry in the inspected source.

evidence.finding: The law distinguishes natural reaches from canalised, piped and drained reaches and requires at least five metres of sanitary access along altered sections.
evidence.reason: Defines river-management classes but not a complete centreline.

evidence.finding: SATC publishes the river within a seven-microbasin diagnostic programme and identifies Rio Criciúma as part of the wider urban drainage system.
evidence.reason: The site supplies basin and report context; route geometry still needs extraction and review.

evidence.sourceName: Wikimedia Commons – Rio Criciúma at Rua Henrique Lage
evidence.finding: The file records camera coordinates -28.679172, -49.376008 for a visible river reach at Rua Henrique Lage.
evidence.reason: The point verifies one observation location only, not the whole linear river record.

decision.blockedReason: The place identity and source base are sufficient for production, but exact current geometry or a documented access/observation anchor is incomplete.
decision.nextAction: Capture the required polygon, centreline, entrance or access anchor and re-run coordinate review.

notes: The current coordinate is an observation anchor, not a river midpoint.
The future geometry should preserve open, culverted, piped and natural segments rather than hiding them behind one point.
